key: All that are in the heavens and the earth entreat Him. Every day He exerciseth (universal) power.
s: Between the passing of all on earth and a warning to jinn and men, the surah turns to prayer; Ibn Kathir, on 55:26 to 55:30, reads it as God needing none and all creatures needing Him every moment, asking by their state and their speech.

evidence.words: وَهَذَا إِخْبَارٌ عَنْ غِنَاهُ عَمَّا سِوَاهُ وَافْتِقَارِ الْخَلَائِقِ إِلَيْهِ فِي جَمِيعِ الْآنَاتِ، وَأَنَّهُمْ يَسْأَلُونَهُ بِلِسَانِ حَالِهِمْ وَقَالِهِمْ، وَأَنَّهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شأن.
evidence.gloss: This is a report of His freedom from need of anything besides Him, and of all creatures’ need of Him at every moment, and that they ask Him with the tongue of their state and of their speech, and that every day He is about some matter.
evidence.licence: classical text public domain; digitisation by Tarteel (QUL), no licence stated; short excerpt with attribution

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Ar-Rahman 55:29, at 4929). Ibn Kathir’s one comment on 55:26 to 55:30 says in his own voice, under ‘yasʾaluhu man fi al-samawat’, that this reports God’s freedom from need of all else and the need of all creatures for Him at every moment, and that they ask Him by the tongue of their state and of their speech; the sentence paraphrases exactly that and cites the comment as on the passage. Plain sense places the ayah between ‘everyone that is thereon will pass away’ (55:26) and the address to man and jinn (55:31 to 55:33), faithful to day.js. Entry-check ok, no changes.
